name: Warehousing and 3PL

problems.words: Client says they sent more cartons than we counted
quick_ideas: Count every inbound against the client's packing list before signing, so gaps are raised at the dock
Photograph damaged or short cartons on arrival, so you have proof.

workzap_build.text: an inbound receiving check that would count against the advance shipping notice, capture damage photos and send the client a discrepancy report the same day.

problems.ask_first: Does the count differ mostly on a few clients, or across all inbound deliveries?
problems.free_stops: The receiving steps are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many inbound cartons arrive with unclear marks or mixed items this week, so dispute patterns show at receiving.
Give one receiver the job of noting shortages in one dock notebook, so every disputed inbound has the same record.

problems.words: Pickers can't find items because they were put in the wrong place
quick_ideas: Label every bin, so locations can be checked
Have putaway confirmed with the location written down, so stock is findable.

workzap_build.text: A location-based stock register with bin labels and putaway confirmation.

problems.ask_first: Is the wrong placing mostly done by new staff, or at busy times?
problems.free_stops: The location scheme is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every time a picker finds stock in a different bay than expected this week, so the worst putaway errors stand out.
Give one putaway lead one location correction list by the dispatch desk, so misplaced stock gets fixed from one place.

problems.words: Wrong items get shipped to the client's customers
quick_ideas: Sort pick lists by location, so pickers walk less and grab less wrongly
Add a second check on high-value orders before sealing.

workzap_build.text: Pick lists sorted by location with scan-to-confirm, catching wrong items before packing.

problems.ask_first: Are the wrong items mostly from similar-looking products, or from picks at busy times?
problems.free_stops: The pick and check flow is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which client orders need item swaps or returns after dispatch this week, so the biggest packing problem is clear.
Give one pack bench lead the final order sheet at sealing time, so the last check happens on every parcel.

problems.words: We don't charge clients for all the handling we actually do
quick_ideas: Log every extra activity for a week (labelling, repacking, extra labour) per client, so you see what goes unbilled
Agree in writing with clients what counts as billable handling.

workzap_build.text: Activity-based billing that captures storage days, pallets, picks, packs and labelling automatically into a monthly invoice per client.

problems.ask_first: Which extra handling goes unbilled most often, labelling, repacking or extra labour?
problems.free_stops: How activities are captured and priced into invoices is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each relabelling, repacking and extra touch by client for one week, so missed handling charges are easy to spot.
Give one person one running list of non-standard client work near dispatch, so chargeable tasks get captured before billing.

problems.words: Billing each client every month takes days in Excel
quick_ideas: List every sheet that feeds billing, so you see where the days go
Pick one client to bill from a single sheet next month, as a test.

workzap_build.text: A billing view that pulls all logged activity per client into one draft invoice ready each month-end.

problems.ask_first: Do you bill from many sheets per client, or just a few?
problems.free_stops: How the billing data is joined is mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down every billing item your team retypes from paper or chat this month, so the slowest part of billing is clear.
Give one billing owner one master list for each client's charge items all month, so month-end collation takes less chasing.

problems.words: Clients want live stock reports and we send Excel once a week
quick_ideas: Ask your top clients which few numbers they actually want, so reports are useful
Send those numbers more often for one client, as a test.

workzap_build.text: a client WhatsApp report or web page giving live stock, orders shipped and inbound status.

problems.ask_first: Do clients want stock figures daily, or only when they plan new orders?
problems.free_stops: What each client sees is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which stock questions each client asks between weekly reports this week, so you see what updates they actually need.
Give one account coordinator one shared list of client stock updates to send each afternoon, so replies stop slipping.

problems.words: Expired or near-expiry goods get shipped because FEFO isn't followed
quick_ideas: List batches near expiry for each client, so they can be picked first
Mark expiry dates clearly at the location.

workzap_build.text: FEFO picking rules and expiry alerts per client batch.

problems.ask_first: Does near-expiry stock affect a few clients, or most of them?
problems.free_stops: Alert rules per client are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many picks this week came from newer batches while older stock was still on hand, so FEFO misses show.
Give one picker lead one near-expiry list at the start of each shift, so older batches get checked before newer ones.

problems.words: Our WMS doesn't connect to clients' Shopify or marketplace accounts
quick_ideas: Count how many client orders are retyped by hand from messages or emailed files this week, so manual order load is clear.
Give one coordinator one order intake notebook for all non-connected clients, so copied orders stop getting missed between channels.

workzap_build.text: Order intake that accepts client spreadsheets or connects to Shopify and marketplaces, so orders arrive without retyping.

problems.ask_first: Do most clients sell on Shopify, or on a mix of marketplaces?
problems.free_stops: Which connections are made is mapped in the solution document.
quick_ideas_original: List which clients send orders by email, WhatsApp or spreadsheet, so you see the retyping load
Ask the busiest clients which store platforms they use.

problems.words: Daily-wage labour don't turn up on peak days
quick_ideas: Confirm workers the night before each peak day, so gaps are known in time
Keep a standby list, so there's someone to call.

workzap_build.text: Shift scheduling with confirmations and reminders, planned from clients' sale calendars.

problems.ask_first: Does the no-show come up mostly on a few days, or at random?
problems.free_stops: The scheduling rules are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which peak shifts had the biggest no-show gaps this month, so the hardest labour days become visible early.
Give one supervisor one attendance list checked at a fixed evening time, so next-day labour gaps are known before the rush.

problems.words: I don't know which clients are profitable for the space they take
quick_ideas: Compare one client's revenue against the space and labour they used last month, so you have a first view
Note clients with lots of handling but low fees.

workzap_build.text: A client profitability view of revenue vs space and labour used, refreshed monthly.

problems.ask_first: Do you track space used per client now, or only revenue?
problems.free_stops: How costs are assigned to clients is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which clients use the most floor space and extra handling this week, so low-earning accounts stand out sooner.
Give one supervisor a single notebook for all client handling extras, so billing reviews stop missing busy accounts.

problems.words: No one does the daily housekeeping and safety checklist properly
quick_ideas: Use the checklist your safety adviser gives you, so the content is right
Name who does it each shift.

workzap_build.text: A daily phone checklist with photo proof per item, with missed checks flagged to the manager.

problems.ask_first: Is the checklist skipped mostly on night shifts, or on all shifts?
problems.free_stops: How the checklist is run and reported is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the completed checklist against one walk round each shift, so missed housekeeping tasks are spotted the same day.
Give one shift lead the checklist board at a fixed handover time, so daily checks actually get signed and reviewed.

never_say: Anything on fire safety, racking ratings, forklift certification or hazardous goods storage.
Bonded or free-zone rules and customs releases; refer to their clearing agent or the authority.
Help adjusting client stock records to hide losses, or storing prohibited or undeclared goods.
Labour or agency staffing law and visas.
Storing client end-customer names or addresses. For fire, racking collapse or injury, emergency services (1122/16, 997/999, 911) come first.

sample_reply.person: We run a 3PL with around twenty clients and monthly billing takes my accountant most of a week. Can this be fixed?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, billing can be made much lighter, and you can start this week. 1. List every sheet that feeds billing, so you can see exactly where the days go. 2. Log a week of extra handling per client, so you can see what currently goes unbilled. Workzap can do this automatically for you: storage, picks, packs and labelling captured as they happen and turned into each client's monthly invoice. Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
